reasons.specificity: The audit closely tracks Harris’s consequential comparisons—Horkheimer/Honneth, monism/light, recognition/impersonal capitalism, colonial recognition, and competing critical methods—with their distinct inferential roles.
reasons.anchoring: Nearly all quoted anchors occur verbatim and support the bounded interpretations, though F27’s “anchor-verified: no” conflicts with an anchor that does occur in the article.
reasons.non_obviousness: It repeatedly makes valuable distinctions between departure and falsity, insufficiency and irrelevance, loss of distinctiveness and impossibility, and scope defeat and categorical rejection.
reasons.coherence: The main table, prose, and ledger align, but the scope assessment contains contradictory metadata about complete review versus lost evidence, and the counter-evidence item on disciplinary use is incorrectly linked to F11.
reasons.usefulness: The comparison-to-verdict table and qualified conclusions are highly useful with the text open, but the artifact is far from compact and repeats the same findings across prose, ledger, counter-evidence, and scope sections.
reasons.hallucination_risk: It carefully limits itself to Harris’s article and flags uninspected external works, with only minor risks from article-level silence claims and wording such as “source-supported” for externally attributed alternatives.

score.one_line: A highly specific and well-anchored comparative audit whose nuanced scoped verdicts are weakened mainly by excessive repetition and internally inconsistent verification metadata.
